sections.title: Russia's War Against Ukraine: Origins, Escalation, and the Struggle for Europe's Security Order
sections.description: This course examines Russia's war against Ukraine — from its historical roots through the 2014 seizure and occupation of Crimea and the Donbas, Russia’s invasion of February 2022, Ukraine’s remarkable defenses, the international coalition that armed Ukraine to fight, the grinding war of attrition that followed, and the contested question of how, and on what terms, the war might end. The course frames the conflict as three elements inextricably intertwined: a Russian war for global power, a Ukrainian war of national survival, and a test of American leadership and NATO unity. The focus will be on the war since 2014, with grounding in the post-Cold War shift in geopolitics that brought Putin to power within Russia to re-establish an authoritarian state, a democratic Ukraine with a path to Europe, and a Europe uncertain how to balance both. Course sessions will trace the 2014–2015 “first invasion” and its unresolved legacies; the intelligence and diplomatic run-up to the 2022 invasion; Ukraine's defense of Kyiv and the reshaping of transatlantic military assistance; the architecture of Western military support (the Ukraine Defense Contact Group, how the Pentagon organized the largest donation of military assistance to a country at war since World War II); the shift to a war of attrition from 2022 through 2024; the material and political toll of the fighting; why Russia and Ukraine each continue to battle; and the range of future scenarios. Readings will balance scholarly, policy, and government sources. They will be supplemented by selections from the instructor’s unpublished book manuscript on the conflict.
